recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. If this library still needs to be listed, maintain it on the HL7 Confluence Open Source Implementations page or another current external registry rather than in FHIR core source.
issue_request: FHIR-12626 was a Published/Persuasive DSTU2 FHIR-I request to add the Efferent Health FHIR-dotnetcore DSTU2 .NET Core entities/schema library to the open-source FHIR implementations list. Jira records the resolution as "Add this (pre-applied)" and comments that it was already done.
initial_application: No current core source entry for FHIR-dotnetcore or Efferent Health, and no FHIR-core commit mentioning FHIR-12626, was found. The Jira application note appears to refer to a then-current external open-source implementations list rather than a durable embedded entry in current core source.
additional_context: The current Implementation Support Module links to the HL7 Confluence Open Source Implementations page instead of maintaining an embedded library table. Later issue FHIR-31735 and commit e404ccd07129409bf907b904ae62ded6c82d28bf intentionally removed embedded reference implementation and tool tables from core source and replaced them with Confluence links.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. Adding an individual DSTU2-era library entry to current FHIR core source would conflict with the later Confluence-list policy and add stale ecosystem-maintenance content to the specification.

related_jiras.note: Its applied resolution moved Reference Implementations and Implementation Tools from embedded spec tables to Confluence-linked pages, explaining why no individual library entry should be added to current core source.

evidence_items.summary: Published/Persuasive DSTU2 request to add the Efferent Health FHIR-dotnetcore library to the open-source FHIR implementations list, recorded as pre-applied.
evidence_items.learned: This establishes the final request and that Jira considered the listing already added at the time.

evidence_items.summary: The current Reference Implementations section links to the HL7 Confluence Open Source Implementations page instead of listing individual libraries.
evidence_items.learned: Current core source already provides the maintained location for open-source implementation listings without embedding product-specific entries.

evidence_items.summary: The Implementation Support module is referenced from current module navigation source.
evidence_items.learned: The inspected implementation-support source is part of the current specification surface.

evidence_items.summary: Applying FHIR-31735 removed embedded reference implementation and tool tables from implsupport-module.html and replaced them with Confluence links.
evidence_items.learned: Later source history intentionally moved implementation listings out of core source, so re-adding an individual library now would be inconsistent.

evidence_items.summary: Published/Persuasive with Modification issue whose resolution moved Reference Implementations and Implementation Tools to Confluence-linked pages.
evidence_items.learned: This later WG-approved issue confirms the current external-list policy for implementation tooling and libraries.

evidence_items.command: git log --grep='FHIR-12626'; git log -S'FHIR-dotnetcore'; rg -i 'FHIR-dotnetcore|Efferent' source; bun run confluence:search refs jira FHIR-12626; bun run zulip:search fts '"FHIR" "12626"'
evidence_items.summary: No core commit or current source entry was found; Confluence refs had no FHIR-12626 hits; Zulip had only a tracker bot notification.
evidence_items.learned: No discovered evidence requires or supports adding a current core source entry for the old DSTU2 library request.
